voice: Dignified, formal, and resolute about Egypt's claim to its antiquities.
notes: PLAY-037: Act 3+ introduction without the ankh he no longer wears (case 82; D-042 reserves +100 and +200 for Ask topics, and Talk intro case 80 + 200 would overflow a one-byte condition), and reactions to being shown his ankh (verb 31) and the real Dagger (verb 22).

entries.text: Good evening.  I'm Laura Bow with the New Orleans Tribune.
Dr. Ptahsheptut Smith, of the Cairo Museum. I find it distasteful to celebrate theft in the name of scholarship. The Egyptian artifacts in this museum belong in Egypt.
The museum would say those artifacts were legally acquired.
A legal document can make possession lawful without making it just. Those who profit from Egypt's dead should remember that history has a long memory.
That is my ankh! Where did you find it?
I think I'll hang on to it for now.
It is mine, Miss Bow. I shall expect it returned.
The Dagger of Amon Ra! Miss Bow, that belongs to Egypt. Give it to me.
Then I shall press Egypt's claim with the authorities. It will come home.
